claims.claim: Movable-type printing existed in Asia centuries before Gutenberg; the first movable type was invented by Bi Sheng in China in the 11th century.
claims.episode_span: not the idea of printing, which had existed in Asia for centuries
claims.supporting_quote: The first movable type was invented by the Chinese artisan Bi Sheng in the 11th century

claims.claim: Gutenberg's type metal was an alloy of lead, tin, and antimony that produced durable, reusable type.
claims.episode_span: First came the type metal alloy—roughly lead with tin and antimony—that could be cast repeatedly into crisp, reusable letters
claims.supporting_quote: He was the first to make type from an alloy of lead, tin, and antimony. The alloy produced durable type suitable for high-quality printing and was better suited to the process than other known materials.

claims.claim: Gutenberg's own innovations included a hand mould for casting type and an oil-based ink suited to metal type.
claims.episode_span: Third was an oil-based ink that would adhere to metal yet transfer cleanly to paper under pressure
claims.supporting_quote: Gutenberg integrated these four technologies into a single working system and added a number of innovations of his own, including a hand mold for casting type and an oil-based ink suited to metal type.

claims.claim: The screw press Gutenberg adapted was an ancient device used for pressing grapes for wine and olives for oil.
claims.episode_span: Fourth was the screw press, adapted from existing wine and olive presses
claims.supporting_quote: Introduced in the 1st century AD by the Romans, it was commonly employed in agricultural production for pressing grapes for wine and olives for oil.

claims.claim: Paper was substantially cheaper than parchment (about one-sixth the price as Italian papermaking centers multiplied), and papermaking reached Germany about a century after spreading in late-13th-century Italy, i.e., in the fourteenth century.
claims.episode_span: Even when paper began to replace parchment in the fourteenth century, the cost reduction stayed modest
claims.supporting_quote: Papermaking centers began to multiply in the late 13th century in Italy, reducing the price of paper to one-sixth of parchment and then falling further. These centers reached Germany a century later.

claims.claim: The real price of books fell sharply after the invention of the printing press.
claims.episode_span: Within a generation the price of an ordinary book fell by roughly an order of magnitude
claims.source_title: Historic trends in book production - AI Impacts
claims.supporting_quote: The real price of books dropped precipitously following the invention of the printing press, but the longer term trend is sufficiently ambiguous that this may not represent a substantial discontinuity.
